evals.prompt: Connect my existing Lambda function to a new Amazon API Gateway REST API.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Asks for all required parameters (`lambda_function_name` and `api_name`) upfront in a single prompt while listing optional parameters with their sensible defaults (`region`, `stage_name='dev'`, `resource_path='invoke'`, `http_method='POST'`, `authorization_type='AWS_IAM'`, `enable_api_key=false`, `enable_cors=false`)
Does not fabricate resource names or execute mutating API Gateway creation calls before receiving parameters and confirmation

evals.prompt: Check in `ap-south-1` (read-only) whether Lambda function `orders-lookup-fn` exists first; if it doesn't exist yet, report that cleanly and provide the complete step-by-step REST API Gateway proxy integration runbook (`api_name=orders-rest-api`, `stage_name=dev`, `resource_path=orders`, `http_method=POST`, `authorization_type=AWS_IAM`, `enable_api_key=true`, `enable_cors=true`) without mutating AWS.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill and checks `lambda:GetFunction` for `orders-lookup-fn` in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands

Reports accurately that `orders-lookup-fn` was not found (aborting live mutation per SOP) and lays out the exact sequence: `create-rest-api`, `get-resources`, `create-resource`, `put-method` (`AWS_IAM` + `apiKeyRequired`), `put-integration` (`type=AWS_PROXY`, integration `httpMethod=POST`), `lambda add-permission` scoped to the exact API source ARN, CORS `OPTIONS` mock integration, stage access logging/throttling, and `create-deployment`
Makes zero mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: After wiring our Python Lambda to API Gateway with `AWS_PROXY`, every request returns `502 Bad Gateway` even though CloudWatch Lambda logs show our function succeeded and returned `{"orderId": 123, "items": ["book"]}`! Explain why and show the exact proxy response structure required.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Explains that `AWS_PROXY` requires the Lambda handler to return an envelope containing `statusCode` (integer), `headers` (object), and `body` as a **JSON-serialized string** (`json.dumps(...)`, plus optional `isBase64Encoded`), NOT a raw dictionary

evals.prompt: API Gateway test-invoke in the Console works, or fails with `Execution failed due to configuration error: Invalid permissions on Lambda function` (`500 Internal Server Error`) when called via the deployed `https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/dev/orders` URL! Diagnose the `lambda:add-permission` source ARN pitfall and show the exact fix.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Explains that API Gateway requires a resource-based policy on the Lambda function (`lambda:InvokeFunction` for principal `apigateway.amazonaws.com`) with `--source-arn arn:aws:execute-api:<region>:<account>:<api-id>/<stage>/<method>/<resource-path>` (or `/*/<method>/<resource-path>` so both Console test-invoke and deployed stage invocations match)

evals.prompt: We enabled `OPTIONS` on our API Gateway REST API resource, so preflight `OPTIONS` returns `200`, yet `fetch('https://.../dev/invoke', { method: 'POST' })` in Chrome STILL fails with `No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource`! Explain why `AWS_PROXY` ignores integration response header mappings on `POST` and show the complete CORS fix.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Explains that while `MOCK` integration handles `OPTIONS` preflight headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`), with **`AWS_PROXY` integration on `POST`/`GET`, the Lambda function itself MUST return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` inside its response `headers` object** (and `GatewayResponses` for `4XX`/`5XX`)

evals.prompt: An engineer wants to deploy an API Gateway REST API connected to Lambda straight to `stage_name=prod` with `authorization_type=NONE`, `enable_api_key=false`, unlimited burst rate, and access logging disabled. Audit this against our connection procedure's security hardening controls.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Recommends enforcing authentication (`AWS_IAM`, `COGNITO_USER_POOLS`, or `CUSTOM` Lambda authorizer rather than unauthenticated `NONE`), CloudWatch access logging (`accessLogSettings`), and Usage Plan / stage throttling (`burstLimit` & `rateLimit`) with API keys where client metering is needed

evals.prompt: Why did `aws apigateway put-integration --type AWS_PROXY --http-method GET --integration-http-method GET` fail or break Lambda invocation when wiring a `GET /items` REST API method to Lambda?
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Explains that the backend Lambda `Invoke` API ALWAYS requires `--integration-http-method POST` regardless of whether the client-facing API Gateway method (`--http-method`) is `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, or `DELETE`

evals.prompt: Compare the four `authorization_type` options (`AWS_IAM`, `COGNITO_USER_POOLS`, `CUSTOM`, `NONE`) when connecting a Lambda function to an API Gateway REST API, and show how caller identity reaches `event.requestContext.authorizer` / `identity` in Lambda.
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Compares `AWS_IAM` (SigV4 workload/service-to-service callers -> `event.requestContext.identity.userArn`), `COGNITO_USER_POOLS` (end-user JWT claims -> `event.requestContext.authorizer.claims`), `CUSTOM` (TOKEN/REQUEST Lambda authorizer -> `event.requestContext.authorizer`), and `NONE` (public unauthenticated — requires explicit rate limiting/WAF justification)

evals.prompt: We updated our API Gateway REST API method authorization and CORS headers via `put-method` and `put-integration-response`, but calling the `/dev/invoke` stage URL still behaves like the old configuration! Why?
expectations: Activates the connecting-lambda-to-api-gateway skill

Explains that in API Gateway REST APIs (v1), editing resources/methods/integrations modifies the unreleased API model only — you MUST call `apigateway create-deployment --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name dev` to publish changes to the live stage

evals.prompt: Verify via AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools how API Gateway **API Keys** (`x-api-key`) work with **Usage Plans** (`create-usage-plan` + `create-usage-plan-key`) and why AWS documentation states API keys must not be used as the sole authentication/authorization mechanism.
expectations: Queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`) with zero raw `aws` CLI commands
Details how API Gateway Usage Plans (`create-usage-plan` with throttle/quota) and Usage Plan Keys (`create-usage-plan-key`) bind API keys to stages where methods require an API key
Confirms AWS's security guidance: API keys identify/meter client applications for throttling and quotas, NOT user authentication/authorization (pair with `AWS_IAM`, Cognito, or Lambda Authorizers)
